title: Labelled affine SNC charts with integral deepest stratum
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ a reduced strict normal crossings boundary with its finite labelled components [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. For $I\subseteq A$ put $Y_I=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\notin I}D_a$ and let $S=(\bigcap_{i\in I}D_i)\cap Y_I$ have its reduced structure. There is a finite family of affine open subschemes $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y_I$ whose intersections with $S$ cover $S$, such that $B$ is a regular Noetherian domain, $V$ is separated, each pulled-back $D_i$ has ideal $(t_i)$, and at every point of $V$ the subtuple of the $t_i$ vanishing there extends to a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. With $J=(t_i)_{i\in I}$, $S\cap V=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ is nonempty integral regular, hence connected. For empty $S$ use the empty family; for $I=\varnothing$ the intersection means $Y$, $J=0$, and $S\cap V=V$.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p.118; Stacks 00NR (algebra.tex, lemma-regular-quotient-regular); agent affine-component refinement of the regular-intersection criterion.

proof.text: Regularity makes Y locally Noetherian and finite type over the field makes it quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. For J equal to the sum of the selected component ideals, the supplied intersection condition makes J.subscheme regular. It is reduced. The kernel of its closed immersion is the vanishing ideal of its closed image; hence J equals J.radical. This identifies the scheme-theoretic intersection with the required reduced structure without a uniqueness construction.

source.place: Tags 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian), 0569 (lemma-regular-normal); ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p.118

proof.text: For a singleton component intersection the stalk quotient is regular of codimension one. The regular-quotient kernel-parameters theorem gives an initial parameter sequence generating its kernel; the quotient dimension formula forces its length to be one. IsRegularImmersion.of_stalk spreads this regular generator to affine neighbourhoods. For finitely many labelled components take their common open neighbourhood and then an affine open inside it. Restriction of ideal sheaves preserves their principal generators, giving actual ideal equalities for all the labels simultaneously.

At each point, filter the ordered equation list to the vanishing labels K. Its germs generate precisely the kernel of the surjective map from the ambient stalk R to the regular K-intersection stalk S. Choose a minimal finite generating set of the maximal ideal of S and lift its list through this surjection. Appending these lifts to the labelled equations generates the maximal ideal of R: map the generated ideal to the maximal ideal of S, pull back, and use that it contains the kernel. The number of lifts is dim S by regularity, so the concatenated list has length |K|+dim S=dim R by the intersection hypothesis. It is a regular parameter system with the required ordered sublist. The affine stalk localization equivalence transports both the list and the vanishing criterion to B_q.

source.place: Proof of Tag 00NR; etale.tex Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), converse proof

proof.text: Apply the existing regular normal decomposition to Y and J.subscheme. Choose the clopen integral components through the point in each. The image of the complement of the chosen intersection component is closed under the closed immersion. Intersect its complement with the chosen ambient component and with the complement of all unselected divisors. Choose the common affine neighbourhood from Step 2 inside this open. Its open immersion into the ambient integral component makes it integral. The affine intersection chart factors by an open immersion through the chosen integral intersection component and contains the original point, hence is integral too.

For the resulting affine open U, its ring B is Noetherian and its prime localizations are the regular stalks, so B is regular. Integrality gives that B is a domain. The sum of the labelled principal ideals is J(U). The affine subscheme-cover pullback square, composed with the quotient-ring equivalence for this equality, gives the residual isomorphism over Spec B. Since J.radical=J from Step 1 this is exactly the radical-intersection pullback in the statement. Its quotient spectrum is integral by Step 4 and regular because it is an open subscheme of the regular intersection, and therefore connected. The affine terminal morphism is separated. If I is empty, the ideal is zero, the quotient homomorphism is bijective, and its spectrum is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian); affine description of closed subschemes and integrality

proof.text: Construct one such chart at each point of the stratum. Their open images cover it. The underlying Noetherian space makes every subset compact, so choose a finite subcover and enumerate its indices by a finite ordinal. Each chosen chart retains all the established properties. For the empty stratum choose the empty indexed family; the empty selected-component case is already covered by the zero-ideal calculation in Step 5.

Step 4: two regular-normal component refinements and the affine basis give integral V and S∩V. Restricting the ideal equalities to an arbitrary affine V is elementary via the closed-immersion affine description (advisory only). Step 5: B is Noetherian, regular and a domain, Spec(B/J) is integral regular hence connected, and V is separated as affine-source. Step 6: DCC makes S quasi-compact, giving a finite subfamily; the S=∅ and I=∅ cases are handled. lean.statement: theorem exists_sncAffineStratumCharts (k : Type u) [Field k] (Y : Scheme.{u}) (y : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType y] [QuasiCompact y] [IsSeparated y] (hY : IsRegularScheme Y) (D : Y.IdealSheafData) (hD : IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary D) (a : ℕ) (C : Fin a → Y.IdealSheafData) (hC : Function.Injective (fun i ↦ (C i).support) ∧ (∀ i, IsIntegral (C i).subscheme ∧ IsRegularScheme (C i).subscheme) ∧ D.support = ⨆ i, (C i).support ∧ ∀ s : Finset (Fin a), ∀ z : (⨆ i ∈ s, C i).subscheme, IsRegularScheme (⨆ i ∈ s, C i).subscheme ∧ ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk ((⨆ i ∈ s, C i).subschemeι z)) = ringKrullDim ((⨆ i ∈ s, C i).subscheme.presheaf.stalk z) + (s.card : ℕ)) (I : Finset (Fin a)) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (Q : Fin n → SNCAffineStratumChart C I), (∀ x : Y, x ∈ (⨆ i ∈ I, C i).support → (∀ i : Fin a, i ∉ I → x ∉ (C i).support) → ∃ (j : Fin n) (z : Spec (Q j).B), (Q j).v z = x) ∧ ((¬ ∃ x : Y, x ∈ (⨆ i ∈ I, C i).support ∧ ∀ i : Fin a, i ∉ I → x ∉ (C i).support) → n = 0)
lean.note: SNCAffineStratumChart packages precisely one chart in the theorem; all data are explicit structure fields. The reduced intersection is pulled back from Y along an open immersion whose image avoids the unselected components, equivalently the reduced stratum of Y_I. This avoids a dependency on the downstream universal-residual-chart module.
